Anita (eng-runtime): seeing a throughput collapse on prod-rt-2 starting ~08:12 UTC, lots of worker restarts and GPU OOMs
Lee (eng-sre): noticed increased tail latency and many restarts, alert page shows 50% drop in qps :eyes:
Anita (eng-runtime): initial correlates point to the recent prefetch threshold tweak (PR #4217) that raised kv prefetch window from 32->64
Mike (eng-ml): that change was to improve cold-cache latency by prefetching more cached KV pages, right?
Anita (eng-runtime): yes, but we see memory churn leading to fragmentation. GPUs hit OOM during large batches and then workers restart after failed allocs
infra-bot: deploy detected: pr-4217 rolled out to canary then to prod at 07:58 UTC
Lee (eng-sre): stack traces in the logs show repeated cudaMalloc failures: "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 1.34GiB"
jess (eng-platform): rolling back can be quick, but want to confirm root cause before flip. any perf profiles?
Anita (eng-runtime): attaching sampling output snippet from hpc-profiler:
```
pid=4321 sample: kernel=matmul_opt, seq_len=2048, free_mem=2.1GB, frag=0.68
kv_prefetch_window=64 -> increased resident set for kvcache by ~1.1GB per worker
alloc failure at alloc(1374389535) -> fallback to host staging then worker restart
```
Mike (eng-ml): kv cache resident growth lines up with traffic pattern: many long-context chat requests around 08:10 causing large KV fills
Lee (eng-sre): noisy tenant effect exacerbated it — we had a tenant surge on dedicated-gpu-3 at same time (see infra dashboard link: https://dash.internal/redwood/prod-rt-2)
Anita (eng-runtime): batcher logs show batch sizes increased after prefetch because prefetching kept KV hot and allowed larger continuous batches: batch_size median 12 -> 20
jess (eng-platform): so combo = higher batch sizes + more KV pages pinned -> higher transient GPU memory -> fragmentation -> OOM on alloc path
Anita (eng-runtime): exactly. Also kernel selection moved to matmul_opt which is slightly more peak-mem hungry for long seqs; kernel-router chose it because throughput looked better in perf table
Mike (eng-ml): we have a perf regression where the kernel heuristic optimized for throughput but didn't consider worst-case resident set with kv prefetching
Lee (eng-sre): action plan?
Anita (eng-runtime): immediate mitigation: revert prefetch window to 32 on prod and force kernel-router to prefer low-mem matmul fallback for seq_len>=1024
jess (eng-platform): starting rollback now for prod-rt-2 (will take ~3m), posting status
infra-bot: rollback initiated for pr-4217 at 08:24 UTC, target ros: prod-rt-2
Anita (eng-runtime): mid-term: add a memory-aware kernel score that adds a resident_set_penalty term when kv resident > threshold
Mike (eng-ml): plus add a dynamic prefetch cap that scales with free_gpu_memory and current batcher queue depth
Lee (eng-sre): and add a guard on worker restarts: if a worker OOMs X times in Y minutes we quarantine node instead of full restart to avoid restart storms
Anita (eng-runtime): I'll open follow-up tickets: 1) kernel scoring change, 2) prefetch cap, 3) quarantine guard, 4) improved metrics linking kv cache resident and kernel selections
jess (eng-platform): rollback complete, qps recovering, worker restarts dropping. monitoring shows fragmentation metric slowly decreasing
Mike (eng-ml): can we capture a reproducible test? maybe replay traffic with long-context sessions and prefetch window 64 to measure worst-case RS and fragmentation rate
Anita (eng-runtime): yes I'll coordinate a repro in staging and include perf snapshots and heap histograms. planning to run overnight load test
Lee (eng-sre): leaving postmortem stub in incidents. Will add timeline and pager hits. tagging oncall for follow-up
Anita (eng-runtime): thanks all. lessons: prefetch heuristics need long-tail memory modeling, kernel heuristics must consider worst-case resident set, and guardrails for noisy tenant surges
Mike (eng-ml): noted. cc @sre on remediation tickets
infra-bot: incident resolved status: degraded->stable at 08:33 UTC (post-rollback).
